analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia
key_insights: US equities fell Friday: S&P 500 -0.52%, Dow -1.23%, Nasdaq -0.21%. Breadth was negative after strong equal-weight outperformance Thursday. S&P and Nasdaq logged modest weekly declines.

WTI settled up 3.8% to above $100/bbl, a third straight weekly gain, with Brent near $114 in Asian trade. Oil was a headwind for consumer groups and, with hot October flash PMI inflation, likely pushed rates higher.

US-Iran conflict: UN ambassador Waltz said it could last another year. The US Navy blockade can continue indefinitely. Officials said no attacks before Election Day, but expectations are elevated for a nearer-term resumption of strikes. Citi cautioned that improved Hormuz flows may reflect inventory drawdowns and that oil risks stay skewed to the upside.

US October flash composite PMI was 57.6 vs 57.3 consensus and 58.4 prior. Manufacturing PMI was 56.0, the highest since May 2022. Selling-price inflation was the highest since Aug 2022. Final October consumer sentiment was 48.0, and year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.7%.

AI trade: semis and memory were higher Friday but neoclouds fell. WDC beat and raised, BE fell 11.2% despite a beat and raise, and FIX fell 9.3% on softer margins. Hyperscaler CDS is at record highs. OpenAI trimmed its valuation target to $1.25T from $1.4T in a roughly $30B raise.

Breadth: the S&P 500 fell 1.2% Thursday while equal-weight RSP rose 0.7%, a 194 bp gap, the largest since July 2024. SOX is down 15% MTD and nearly 27% from its June high, yet about 55% of S&P constituents are above their 50-day average. Goldman noted the largest two-week net selling in Global Info Tech on record, a potential squeeze setup.
The 20-day correlation between Treasury returns and AI stocks turned to -0.56, negative for the first time since March. The cost of hedging further Treasury gains is the highest since March.
Upcoming US catalysts: Mag 7 earnings and the October FOMC meeting, where the Fed is widely expected to hold, then midterms the following week.

French 10-year OAT yield passed 5% for the first time since 2002, reaching 5.142% intraday and closing at 5.090%. The OAT-Bund spread widened to about 175 bps from about 158 bps. Economists warn it could widen by as much as 200 bps, and no ECB intervention is expected.

ECB is expected to hold next week and hike 25 bp in December to a 2.75% deposit rate, while markets price about 75 bp of tightening by end-2027. Eurozone October flash composite PMI fell to 51.9 vs 52.7 expected.

UK: September CPI accelerated to 3.5%, cementing a 5 Nov BoE hike, with markets pricing at least three moves by April 2027. UK composite PMI hit an eight-month high of 53.1, but GfK consumer confidence fell to -24 vs -14 expected. The Budget is on 28 Oct and is expected to be low-key.

European gas hit EUR91-93/MWh, a multi-year high, with storage near 75%, the lowest seasonal level since 2009. Goldman sees about EUR70/MWh by year-end if Gulf flows improve and a cold-winter cap near EUR150.
Europe earnings: Eni, L'Oreal, Holcim, Rexel and Sodexo rose on results. Kering (-16.4%), Volvo Car (-24.2%), Safran (-10.3%) and Valeo (-11.5%) fell sharply.

Asia: Japan September core CPI was 2.1% y/y. Nikkei reported the BOJ will hold at 1.25% on 29-30 Oct, with a December hike possible. China's national team ETF buying lifted the CSI 300 1.7% after it entered a technical bear market Thursday. Australia's composite PMI fell to 47.7.

SK Hynix dropped the US IPO of Solidigm citing market volatility, and other regional IPOs were delayed or scrapped. Crown Castle rose 9.1% on a report that SpaceX is in talks for at least 80K cell sites, which pressured carriers such as Verizon (-1.2%).

market_movers.rationale: Preliminary Q3 EPS and revenue came in below consensus on weak Europe, FY26 guidance was withdrawn and a CEO transition was announced. Stock -22.5%.
Third straight beat and raise with backlog growth, but macro uncertainty, negative FCF and margin pressure flagged. Stock -11.2%.
Q3 earnings and revenue beat with a roughly $4B q/q backlog increase, but margins were softer and the CFO is leaving. Stock -9.3%.
Q3 earnings beat and Talent Solutions returned to growth for the first time since 2022. Stock +21.7%.
Bloomberg reported SpaceX in talks for a minimum of 80K cell sites. Stock +9.1%.
The Information reported the company is exploring a sale and held talks with DASH and UBER. Stock +9.2%.
Q3 earnings beat, new $1.2B buyback, Q4 and FY27 guidance largely above the Street. Stock +8.2%.
Q3 results ahead, subscription growth accelerated and AI-related ARR is about 15% of total. Stock +5.0%.
Wireless carriers fell on SpaceX competition concerns. Stock -1.2%.
Q3 earnings better with revenue in line. Billed-business growth decelerated and about 5% headcount reduction announced. Stock -3.7%.
FQ2 revenue missed, EPS helped by tariff refunds, FY27 revenue guidance cut on softer HOKA and UGG. Stock -4.9%.
Q3 EPS and revenue missed and the FY26 EPS guide was sharply cut after shelving a Q4 loan sale. Stock -10.8%.
Q3 revenue and EPS missed on raw material, logistics and Thailand flooding costs. Stock -3.5%.
Q3 earnings and revenue missed, with delayed launches and trimmed Q4 revenue and margin guidance. Stock -5.0%.
Barclays downgraded Lancashire Holdings to underweight. It forecasts a 2026 dividend of $1.17 (about 10% yield) but sees a less supportive outlook beyond mid-2027 as pricing softens.

earnings_insights: WDC: beat and raised, said demand remains supply constrained, visibility now extends into 2030-31, and downplayed capacity addition concerns (reported Q-results, date not given).
BE: reported a beat and raise, its third in a row, with backlog growth ahead of revenue growth and capacity outlook up to and beyond 5 GW. Flagged negative FCF and margin pressure.
FIX: Q3 earnings and revenue better than expected, backlog up nearly $4B q/q, margins softer, CFO transition, dividend increased.
AXP: Q3 revenue in line, raised the low end of FY EPS guide, reaffirmed revenue guidance.
LKQ: preliminary Q3 EPS and revenue below consensus, FY26 guidance withdrawn.
DECK: FQ2 revenue missed, EPS beat helped by tariff refunds, FY27 revenue guidance cut.
FCNCA: Q3 earnings beat, NII above consensus, NIM below consensus, $1.2B buyback.
RHI: Q3 earnings beat, revenue in line, next-quarter revenue guide brackets consensus.
Eni: Q3 adjusted net profit more than doubled to EUR2.8B (reported), beating consensus, with a EUR1.3B special dividend and 2026 buyback raised 12% to EUR3.8B.
L'Oreal: Q3 like-for-like sales +7.7%, ahead of analyst expectations.
Holcim: Q3 net sales +15.5% to CHF4.66B, recurring EBIT +16.8% to CHF976M, FY organic recurring EBIT growth guidance raised to 10-12%.
Hexagon: Q3 revenue EUR1.05B vs consensus EUR1.01B, EPS EUR0.08 vs EUR0.07 consensus, EBIT EUR26.5M vs consensus EUR262.6M as printed in the report.
Rexel: 9M sales +7.3% to EUR15.44B, FY sales growth guidance raised to about 7% from about 5%.
Safran: Q3 adjusted revenue +14.7% to EUR9.003B, slightly above consensus, but spare-parts growth below forecasts. FY26 guidance maintained.
Kering: Q3 group sales -1% comparable to EUR3.35B, Gucci -6% to EUR1.29B.
Volvo Car: Q3 revenue down 23% to SEK66.9B and a SEK5.6B EBIT loss.
Valeo: Q3 like-for-like sales -2.6% to EUR4.88B, missing consensus.
Saab: Q3 revenue +30.6% organically to SEK20.55B, EBIT +42% to SEK1.95B, order bookings SEK65.83B.
DISCO: Q2 net income missed estimates and Q3 guidance came below consensus.
Upcoming: Mag 7 earnings are next week, per the report.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus was 57.3 and prior 58.4. Second-fastest expansion since Mar 2022, with selling-price inflation the highest since Aug 2022.
In line with consensus, down from 58.8.
Little changed from 46.3. Year-ahead inflation expectations 4.7% and long-run 3.5%, highest since May.
Consensus was 52.7. France was the main drag, with output in contraction partly due to strikes and unrest.
Consensus was 51.7. An eight-month high, with employment growing for the first time since Sept 2024.
Consensus was -14. Biggest drop outside Covid since the 2016 Brexit vote.
Matched expectations, first return to the 2% range this year. Ex fresh food and energy was 2.4% vs 2.3% consensus.
Most economists expect a hold next week and a final 25 bp hike in December. Markets price about 75 bp of tightening by end-2027.
Per a Nikkei report, a hold is expected, with a December hike still possible.

macro_indicators.indicator: JCER consensus Japan core inflation peak
macro_indicators.interpretation: Expected to fade afterwards on a scheduled food consumption tax cut.

crypto_views: Bitcoin futures were off 0.2% in the US session and flat in Europe. Cryptocurrencies were strong in Asia.
risk_factors: Oil near $100 WTI and $114 Brent with a risk of renewed US strikes on Iran.
Higher-for-long inflation: US selling-price inflation at a four-year high and rising consumer inflation expectations.
AI funding and capex scrutiny: Meta capital raise signals, record hyperscaler CDS, and weaker investor demand for OpenAI.
French fiscal credibility and spread widening, with possible contagion to Belgium.
European gas storage at record-low seasonal levels ahead of winter.
Fading China stimulus hopes and uncertain sustainability of state support.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility index closed at 19.45, up 2.21 points on the day and up about 19% MTD.
The cost of hedging against further Treasury gains is the highest since March, with the bond rally amplified by short covering.
Goldman noted the largest two-week net selling in Global Info Tech on record, a potential squeeze facilitator.
BTIG noted a third of trading days this year have seen an S&P 500 decline with positive index breadth, the most of any year back to 1996, and cautioned a higher-correlation selloff could happen.
Hyperscaler CDS is at record highs.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict continues, with a US naval blockade and reports of plans for new US strikes. Iran is reported to be prepared to hit Gulf airports, energy pipelines and civilian infrastructure in response.
Officials say there will be no US attacks before Election Day, while Netanyahu urged joint action to topple the Iranian regime.
Flows through the Strait of Hormuz are holding up and Gulf exports are recovering, per the report.
French political fragmentation, budget paralysis and weekend unrest and violence are driving the bond rout.
The FT reported Washington proposed caps on investments into China's technology and biotech firms.
US midterm elections are due the week after next. Prediction markets price about a 70% chance of Democrats winning the Senate and about 90% for the House.
cross_bank_references: Citi cautioned against extrapolating several days of improved Hormuz flows, with oil risks skewed to the upside.
Goldman Sachs argues European gas is not a repeat of 2022 and sees a base case of about EUR70/MWh by year-end.
Credit Agricole is more cautious on the BoE, expecting a dovish hike that fails to validate the four moves priced.
UniCredit strategists noted foreign holdings of French debt leave scope for further selling.

tension_points.what_invalidates: A higher-correlation selloff, which BTIG cautioned could happen at some time.

tension_points.bear_case: Economists warn spreads could widen by as much as 200 bps before finding a floor, with budget paralysis and unrest and no immediate ECB relief.
